article_title: School-Based Prevention of Problem Behaviors: A Meta-Analysis
citation: Wilson, D.B., Gottfredson, D.C. & Najaka, S.S. (2001). School-Based Prevention of Problem Behaviors: A Meta-Analysis. Journal of Quantitative Criminology. https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1011050217296
title: Meta-analytic evidence base of 165 school-based prevention studies
description: This element is the meta-analytic synthesis itself: a quantitative review of "results from 165 studies of school-based prevention activities that ranged from individual counseling or behavior modification programs through efforts to change the way schools are managed." It covers four outcomes (crime, substance use, dropout/nonattendance, and other conduct problems) and codes program types from counseling and behavior modification through school management changes. The synthesis adjusts for measured method and population differences when comparing effects across studies.
requirements: Studies of school-based prevention activities reporting outcomes for the four problem-behavior domains, synthesized with meta-analytic techniques adjusting for method and population differences
constraints: The article notes that many popular school-based prevention approaches have not been well studied to date, limiting the evidence base
target_learners: School-age children and adolescents in school-based prevention programs
target_learning_goals: Reducing crime and delinquency, alcohol and drug use, dropout and nonattendance, and other conduct problems
examples: The synthesis ranged from individual counseling or behavior modification programs through efforts to change the way schools are managed
key_sources: Wilson, D.B., Gottfredson, D.C. & Najaka, S.S. (2001). School-Based Prevention of Problem Behaviors: A Meta-Analysis. Journal of Quantitative Criminology. https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1011050217296

article_title: Pilot study: the impact of simulation-based pediatric basic life support training on the performance of caregivers of children with Rett syndrome.
citation: Kocyigit S, Akgun-Dogan O, Hatirnaz Ng O, Alanay Y, Guven F. (2026). Pilot study: the impact of simulation-based pediatric basic life support training on the performance of caregivers of children with Rett syndrome. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09158-y
title: 16-step PBLS checklist aligned with 2021 ERC guidelines and developed through the Delphi method
description: A standardized 16-step performance checklist used to assess caregiver PBLS skills before and after simulation training. It was developed through the Delphi method and aligned with the 2021 European Resuscitation Council PBLS Guidelines. Each item is scored as 10 (correct), 5 (partially correct), or 0 (incorrect or omitted), with performance independently assessed by two expert instructors through structured direct observation.
requirements: Two independent expert instructors for reliable scoring
Pediatric mannequins for structured direct observation of performance
constraints: When a step could not be physically demonstrated on the mannequin, correct verbalization by the caregiver was accepted as evidence of appropriate assessment or intent
target_learners: Lay caregivers being assessed on PBLS skills
target_learning_goals: Objective assessment of pediatric basic life support psychomotor skills
examples: Checklist items include checking for consciousness, shouting for help, checking for breathing, opening the airway, delivering 5 rescue breaths, and performing effective chest compressions with specified hand position, technique, depth of 4–5 cm, and rate of 100–120/min
key_sources: Kocyigit S, Akgun-Dogan O, Hatirnaz Ng O, Alanay Y, Guven F. (2026). Pilot study: the impact of simulation-based pediatric basic life support training on the performance of caregivers of children with Rett syndrome. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09158-y

article_title: Cognitive learning versus practical "hands-on" training for acquisition of laparoscopic surgical skills: an optimal combination study.
citation: Cizmic Amila, Schwabe Nils, Häberle Frida, Killat David, Giannou Anastasios D., Preukschas Anas A., Nießen Anna, Pianka Frank, Billmann Franck, Mehrabi Arianeb, Müller-Stich Beat P., Hackert Thilo, Nickel Felix. (2025). Cognitive learning versus practical “hands-on” training for acquisition of laparoscopic surgical skills: an optimal combination study. Surgical Endoscopy. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00464-025-11673-w
title: 16-hour combined CL and PT laparoscopic training curriculum with six cognitive and seven practical modules
description: A predefined 16-hour curriculum of cognitive learning (CL) and practical training (PT) modules "specifically tailored for MIS training in novices." The CL side comprises six units, including e-learning programs for LCHE, tutor-led video analysis, situation awareness training with pop quiz questions, video-frame annotation in LabelMe, a theoretical knowledge test, and the Touch Surgery mobile serious game. The PT side comprises seven modules, including camera guidance, rubber band tasks, cutting and thread-guiding tasks in a Szabo–Berci–Sackier Box Trainer, VR training, and tissue dissection on ex-porcine liver tissue.
requirements: Trained tutors, previously trained by an experienced board-certified surgeon, supervise all modules and ensure designated training time is accurate
constraints: The theoretical knowledge test was not performed in Group 2 due to time limitations of designated CL
target_learners: Medical students in their clinical years without MIS experience
target_learning_goals: Visuospatial and visuomotor cognition, instrument handling, camera guidance, and laparoscopic cholecystectomy procedural skills
examples: Trainees annotated four predefined LCHE video frames (instruments introduced, first cauterization, cystic artery and duct dissected, clipping) in the LabelMe annotation software
